items.question: Does Rediacc run on my own servers?
items.answer: Yes. Rediacc runs on any Linux server with btrfs (an open-source storage system built into Linux) support. Physical servers, virtual machines, and cloud servers (AWS, Azure, GCP, Hetzner, OVH, etc.) are all supported.

items.question: How are machines counted?
items.answer: Each physical or virtual server where Rediacc is installed counts as one machine. Instant copies made on those machines don't count separately. Every self-serve plan covers one machine (one Floating license). Running on more than one machine, including every node of a cluster, is an Enterprise setup sold through our partners, and the node count is agreed at order time.

items.question: What does Enterprise include?
items.answer: Enterprise is built to fit and sold through our partners. Terms are negotiable, workloads run across multiple machines, and it includes dedicated server space, a custom recovery promise, and 24/7/365 support. Plus security reviews and regular drills.

items.question: Is there a free trial?
items.answer: Yes. Professional and Business both start with a 14-day free trial. Both ask for a card at signup so the trial can roll into a subscription, and the first charge only lands when the trial ends. Cancel before then and nothing is charged.

items.question: How does billing work?
items.answer: Both paid plans bill monthly or annually, and annual billing saves 15%. Plans can change at any time: upgrades take effect immediately, downgrades apply at the start of the next billing cycle, and there are no penalties or fees. We accept all major credit cards (Visa, MasterCard, American Express), and Enterprise plans can be invoiced.

items.question: What happens if I cancel?
items.answer: Cancel during the 14-day trial and no charge ever lands. Cancel a paid plan later and its features stay until the end of the billing period, then the account falls back to the free Community plan. Repositories keep running the whole time.

informationWeCollect.title: 2. Information We Collect
content: We collect minimal information necessary to provide our services. The categories of data we collect depend on how you interact with us.

content: When you submit our contact form, we collect your name, email address, subject of inquiry, and message content. This data is sent directly to our email address and is not stored in a database on our servers.

analyticsData.title: 2.3 Analytics Data
content: We use Plausible Analytics, a privacy-focused, cookieless analytics tool. Plausible does not use cookies, does not collect personal data, and is fully compliant with GDPR, CCPA, and PECR. Analytics data includes page views, referral sources, browser type, and country-level location, all without identifying individual visitors.

productTelemetry.title: 2.5 Product Telemetry Data
content: Our software products (CLI and Renet Agent) collect anonymous usage telemetry to improve product quality, performance, and reliability. Telemetry data includes technical information such as application version, operating system, performance metrics, feature usage patterns, and error reports. Personal identifiers are anonymized before collection: email addresses are reduced to domain only, user IDs are hashed and truncated, and passwords or secrets are never collected.
Telemetry is enabled by default in our CLI, and can be disabled in all products. For complete details on what each product collects and how to opt out, see our Telemetry Policy.

cookies.title: 2.4 Cookies
content: We use a single functional cookie (rediacc_lang) to remember your language preference across visits. This cookie is strictly necessary for the website to function as expected and does not track you or collect personal data. For more details, see our Cookie Policy.

Billing records are retained as required by applicable tax and accounting laws.

Product telemetry data is retained as raw traces for up to 90 days for debugging purposes. Aggregated telemetry metrics are retained for up to 12 months and then deleted. For details, see our Telemetry Policy.

meta.description: Details on what telemetry data Rediacc products collect, why, how it is processed, and how to opt out. Covers the CLI and Renet Agent.
meta.keywords: telemetry policy, data collection, OpenTelemetry, opt-out, privacy, GDPR, Rediacc

introduction.title: 1. Introduction
content: Rediacc software products collect anonymized usage telemetry to help us improve product quality, diagnose issues, and understand how our tools are used. This Telemetry Policy describes exactly what data is collected, why, how it is processed, and how you can opt out.
This policy covers two products: the Rediacc CLI and the Rediacc Renet Agent. Website analytics (Plausible) are covered separately in our Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy.

principles.title: 2. Our Telemetry Principles
content: All telemetry collection at Rediacc follows these principles:
items: Privacy by design: Personal identifiers are anonymized before transmission. Email addresses are reduced to domain only, user IDs are hashed (SHA-256) and truncated, passwords and secrets are never collected.
Minimal collection: We collect only what is necessary to improve product quality and diagnose issues. We do not collect file contents, database contents, query results, or business data.
Transparency: This policy lists every category of data collected by each product. There are no hidden data flows.
User control: Every product provides a mechanism to disable telemetry entirely. Opt-out is respected immediately and completely.
Aggregation: Telemetry data is analyzed in aggregate. We do not build individual user profiles from telemetry.

legalBasis.title: 3. Legal Basis for Collection
content: Under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the ePrivacy Directive, our legal basis for telemetry collection depends on the product context:

For the CLI and Renet Agent (installed on your infrastructure): telemetry is collected under legitimate interest (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)) with clear opt-out mechanisms provided. You can disable telemetry before any data is sent.
For users in jurisdictions requiring explicit consent (e.g., South Korea under PIPA), telemetry should be opted into explicitly through the product configuration before any data is transmitted.

cli.title: 4. CLI Telemetry
content: The Rediacc CLI uses the OpenTelemetry Node SDK. Telemetry is transmitted to rediacc.com.

cliDataCollected.title: 4.1 Data Collected
content: The CLI collects the following categories of data:
items: Command usage: command name, CLI version, exit code, success or failure status
Anonymized arguments: command options with sensitive values redacted, so passwords, tokens, secrets, API keys, and credentials are replaced with [REDACTED]
Environment: operating system type, Node.js runtime version, deployment environment
Error information: error type, error message, and limited stack trace when commands fail
API interactions: HTTP method, URL path, response status code, request duration
Session: randomly generated session ID, command execution duration
Performance profiling: CPU usage samples and memory allocation profiles, collected automatically and sent to our profiling endpoint

cliOptOut.title: 4.2 How to Opt Out
content: You can disable CLI telemetry (including profiling) using any of these methods:
items: Set the environment variable REDIACC_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
Set telemetryEnabled: false in your CLI configuration file
Telemetry is automatically disabled in CI environments (detected via the CI environment variable)

bridge.title: 5. Renet Agent Telemetry
content: The Rediacc Renet Agent uses OpenTelemetry with gzip-compressed OTLP export. Telemetry is transmitted to rediacc.com in batches (maximum 10 spans, flushed every 5 seconds).

bridgeDataCollected.title: 5.1 Data Collected
content: The Renet Agent collects the following categories of data:
items: Queue operations: task ID, priority level, operation type, execution duration, success or failure status
SSH operations: target host, username, port number, exit code, execution duration (no command content or output is collected)
API calls: procedure name, request duration
Vault operations: operation type and duration (no secret values, keys, or vault contents are collected)
Renet Agent lifecycle: startup, shutdown, and reconnection events
Performance profiling: CPU usage samples and memory allocation profiles, collected automatically and sent to our profiling endpoint

bridgeOptOut.title: 5.2 How to Opt Out
content: Set the environment variable REDIACC_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 to disable Renet Agent telemetry (including profiling).

dataProcessing.title: 6. Data Processing and Storage
content: All telemetry data is transmitted over encrypted connections (TLS 1.2+) to our telemetry endpoint. Data is processed and stored as follows:
items: Encryption: All data is encrypted in transit using TLS. The Renet Agent additionally uses gzip compression.
Retention: Raw telemetry traces are stored for up to 90 days for debugging and incident investigation. Aggregated metrics are retained for up to 12 months and then deleted.
Access: Telemetry data is accessible only to Rediacc engineering and operations staff on a need-to-know basis.
No third-party sharing: Telemetry data is not shared with, sold to, or accessible by any third party.
Infrastructure: All telemetry data is processed and stored on infrastructure located within the European Union.

internationalTransfers.title: 7. International Data Transfers
content: Telemetry data is processed and stored exclusively on servers within the European Union. items.q: Is this an authoritative translation of the directive?
items.a: No. It is an unofficial English-language summary intended to make the directive's structure and obligations accessible. For binding interpretation, consult the official text at OJ L 333/80 (27 December 2022) or via EUR-Lex (CELEX 32022L2555). National transposition acts in your Member State may impose stricter or differently-scoped obligations than the directive itself.

items.q: Who is in scope under NIS2?
items.a: Companies in Annex I or Annex II sectors that pass the medium-size mark. That means 50+ staff, or more than EUR 10 million in turnover, per Recommendation 2003/361/EC. Annex I covers what the EU treats as the most critical sectors: energy, transport, banking, financial markets, health, water, digital infrastructure, public administration, space. Annex II covers other critical sectors: postal, waste, chemicals, food, manufacturing, digital providers, research. A few entities are in scope no matter their size: TLD registries, DNS providers, trust service providers, and central public administration. Sections 4, 6, and 7 of the PDF cover scope in detail.

items.q: When did NIS2 enter into force, and what is the transposition deadline?
items.a: The directive took effect on 16 January 2023. Member States had until 17 October 2024 to add it to national law. It started to apply on 18 October 2024. That is also the day NIS1 was repealed. The full timeline sits in Section 16. That covers the 17 April 2025 deadline to send entity lists to the Commission, plus the review schedule. Most teams underestimate how much of that timeline is already behind them.

For essential entities: EUR 10,000,000 or 2% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher. For important entities: EUR 7,000,000 or 1.4% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher. The directive also allows penalties beyond fines. As a last resort, regulators can temporarily ban senior leaders at essential entities from their roles. Section 15 covers how fines get set.

items.q: Does NIS2 apply to non-EU companies?
items.a: Yes, in two ways. Directly: non-EU DNS, cloud, data centre, CDN, MSP/MSSP, online marketplace, search, and social-networking providers offering services in the EU must appoint an EU representative and comply. Indirectly: any non-EU supplier providing products or services to EU essential or important entities will be subject to supply-chain security contractual requirements imposed by their EU customers under Article 21(2)(d). Section 17 covers both.

items.q: How does Article 23 incident reporting work?
items.a: Three deadlines, all triggered by "becoming aware" of a significant incident: 24 hours for an early warning, 72 hours for a full incident notification, and one month for the final report. Service recipients must also be notified without undue delay if a significant cyber threat is likely. Section 10 has the full reporting matrix.
